function: Channel estimation: self-supervised U-Net denoiser refines MMSE and Bussgang linear MMSE estimates obtained from low-resolution-ADC pilot signals (pp. 2-4).
system: Single-cell uplink massive MIMO, BS with 64 or 128 antennas and 1-2 bit ADCs, 16-96 single-antenna users, no RIS, 28 GHz (pp. 2, 4).
method: Blind2Unblind U-Net trained self-supervised on a single noisy estimate: global-aware blind-spot mask, re-visible loss, Adam, leaky ReLU, applied after MMSE or BLMMSE (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: DeepMIMO ray-tracing dataset, outdoor scenario O1_28 at 28 GHz, 0.05 GHz bandwidth, 10 paths; 10^3 samples per dataset in the robustness test (pp. 4-5).
test_conditions: Trained on each noisy estimate, no clean labels; SNR sweeps; red-to-blue BS area change tested against DnCNN trained on red (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: MMSE (1-3 bit, full precision), BLMMSE. Learned: denoising autoencoder, DIP, Self2Self, supervised DnCNN (pp. 4-5).
metrics: NMSE (linear and dB), per-epoch FLOPs, memory cost, per-epoch time (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Order O(M x K) for the U-Net; Table II: 0.59G FLOPs, 3.42M memory, 0.38 s per epoch versus supervised DnCNN 0.61T FLOPs, 5.74 s (pp. 4-5).
openness: Public DeepMIMO O1_28 dataset; footnote links the adopted architecture code at https://github.com/kkk-n-bit/nn_architecture (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "We use DeepMIMO to generate the channel dataset at the 28 GHz operating frequency." Scenario O1_28 (p. 4); DeepMIMO ray tracing is on the q1 list. The i.i.d. CN(0,1) assumption on p. 2 only serves the MMSE derivation, the simulations use DeepMIMO.
q2_support: p. 5: "the proposed self-supervised framework shows relative stability" in the red-to-blue test of Fig. 7, but the method trains on each noisy estimate (p. 1: "relying merely on single noisy data"); only the supervised DnCNN is trained on red and tested on blue, so no trained model of the method is tested on an unseen site.
q3_support: p. 4: "we compare the performance of four distinct denoising methods as shown in Fig. 5". Fig. 5 (NMSE) has 1 bit by MMSE (non-learned) and the learned denoising autoencoder [12], DIP [5] and Self2Self [6]; Fig. 7 (p. 5) adds the supervised DnCNN [13].
q4_support: p. 4: "the model involves a computational complexity of" O(M x K). Table II (p. 5, read as image) gives per-epoch FLOPs 0.59G, memory cost 3.42M and per-epoch time 0.38 s for the proposed framework.
q5_support: p. 4: "DeepMIMO is a publicly available dataset generated by the Remcom Wireless Insite tool". The channels are generated from its O1_28 scenario; footnote 2 (p. 4) also links the code of the adopted architecture.
notes: Included: letter with a self-supervised denoiser for channel estimation under low-resolution ADCs, NMSE results on pp. 4-5; MIMO BS, so no single-antenna exclusion. Area 2. q2 is borderline: Fig. 7 (p. 5) shows the method stable after a site change, but the method is trained on the single noisy estimate of each condition and the paper states no pretrained model tested on a new site (Table II per-epoch FLOPs of the method, 0.59G, are about 1/1000 of DnCNN trained on 10^3 samples, 0.61T, consistent with one sample per epoch); the reviewer may read Fig. 7 as a new-site test and flip q2. The footnote link may be the authors' own repository or the code of the borrowed U-Net, the text does not say; q5 holds through the public DeepMIMO dataset. Table II and Figs. 4-7 read as page images. Title on p. 1 matches; DOI printed on p. 1 matches.
